# Mainframe entity refinements

Entity refinements specialize upstream OpenTelemetry entities with additional
identity and description attributes specific to the
Mainframe domain.

| Refinement ID | Refined Entity Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `refinement.mainframe.host` | `host` | Mainframe refinement of the generic host entity for the IBM Z Central Processing Complex (CPC). A CPC is a physical bare-metal server — the mainframe equivalent of any host. The IBM Z-specific attributes (serial number, machine type, machine model) extend the generic host description while preserving full compatibility with consumers that understand the base host entity. |
| `refinement.mainframe.host.virtualization.platform` | `virtualization.platform` | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.platform for the IBM Z Central Processing Complex (CPC). A CPC is a physical computing platform that hosts firmware-enforced logical partitions (LPARs) via PR/SM, directly analogous to virtualization.platform in the generic virtualization schema. |
| `refinement.mainframe.partition.virtualization.partition` | `virtualization.partition` | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.partition for an IBM Z logical partition (LPAR).  An LPAR is a firmware-enforced partition managed by PR/SM, directly analogous to virtualization.partition in the generic virtualization schema. |
| `refinement.mainframe.processor_pool.virtualization.resource_pool` | `virtualization.resource_pool` | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.resource_pool for an IBM Z shared processor pool. A shared processor pool defines a capacity boundary for a group of physical processor engines (CP, IFL, zIIP, ICF) shared by logical partitions, directly analogous to virtualization.resource_pool in the generic virtualization schema. |
| `refinement.mainframe.storage_group.virtualization.storage_pool` | `virtualization.storage_pool` | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.storage_pool for an IBM Z DPM storage group. A storage group aggregates FCP/SCSI or FICON/ECKD volumes allocated to partitions and guests, directly analogous to virtualization.storage_pool in the generic virtualization schema. |
| `refinement.mainframe.vswitch.virtualization.vswitch` | `virtualization.vswitch` | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.vswitch for an IBM z/VM VSWITCH or DPM virtual switch. A mainframe virtual switch bridges partitions and guest VMs to physical OSA-Express or RoCE network adapters, directly analogous to virtualization.vswitch in the generic virtualization schema. |
| `refinement.mainframe.zvm.guest.virtualization.vm` | `virtualization.vm` | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.vm for an IBM z/VM guest virtual machine. A z/VM guest is a virtual machine managed by the z/VM Control Program (CP), running Linux on Z or z/OS, directly analogous to virtualization.vm in the generic virtualization schema. |
| `refinement.mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.virtualization.hypervisor` | `virtualization.hypervisor` | Mainframe refinement of virtualization.hypervisor for the z/VM Control Program (CP). z/VM is a Type-1 software hypervisor that runs on IBM Z hardware (bare-metal or inside a PR/SM LPAR) and manages hundreds to thousands of guest virtual machines, directly analogous to virtualization.hypervisor in the generic virtualization schema. |

**[1] `host.name`:** The name of the Central Processing Complex (CPC) as configured on the HMC. Reported by the HMC Web Services API CPC object field `name`.

**[2] `host.arch`:** SHOULD be set to "s390x" for IBM Z and LinuxONE systems.

**[3] `host.id`:** The host.id SHOULD be the object-id UUID of the Central Processing Complex (CPC) as defined by the HMC Web Services API CPC object.

**[4] `host.type`:** SHOULD be the concatenation of the IBM machine type and model of the Central Processing Complex (CPC), e.g., "9175-ME1".

**[5] `mainframe.host.machine_model`:** IBM machine model tier (e.g. "ME1"). Combined with mainframe.host.machine_type this forms the full type-model string that populates host.type.

**[6] `mainframe.host.machine_type`:** IBM four-digit machine type (e.g. "9175"). Consumers that understand only the base host entity should use host.type instead.

**[7] `mainframe.host.serial_number`:** Mainframe-specific serial number of the CPC. Consumers that understand only the base host entity should use host.id instead.

**[8] `host.ip`:** IPv4 Addresses MUST be specified in dotted-quad notation. IPv6 addresses MUST be specified in the [RFC 5952](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc5952.html) format.

**[9] `host.mac`:** MAC Addresses MUST be represented in [IEEE RA hexadecimal form](https://standards.ieee.org/wp-content/uploads/import/documents/tutorials/eui.pdf): as hyphen-separated octets in uppercase hexadecimal form from most to least significant.

**[10] `host.name`:** The name of the physical computing platform as configured in the platform management interface. For IBM Z systems this is the CPC name as configured on the Hardware Management Console (HMC). Consumers using the generic host entity should use host.name as the primary identifier; virtualization.platform.id may be used as an additional opaque UUID where required.

**[11] `host.arch`:** The CPU architecture of the platform. SHOULD be set to "s390x" for IBM Z and LinuxONE systems.

**[12] `host.id`:** A platform-specific opaque UUID that uniquely identifies this physical platform within its management domain. For IBM Z this corresponds to the CPC object-id as reported by the HMC Web Services API. Consumers that use only the generic host entity should prefer host.id over virtualization.platform.id.

**[13] `host.type`:** The hardware model of the physical platform. For IBM Z systems this is the machine type and model concatenated with a hyphen, e.g., "9175-ME1" for the IBM z16 Model ME1. Consumers that use only the generic host entity should prefer host.type over virtualization.platform.model.

**[14] `mainframe.host.machine_model`:** IBM machine model tier (e.g. "ME1"). Combined with mainframe.host.machine_type, this forms the full type-model string.

**[15] `mainframe.host.machine_type`:** IBM four-digit machine type (e.g. "9175"). Use alongside virtualization.platform.model for cross-platform consumers.

**[16] `mainframe.host.serial_number`:** Mainframe-specific serial number of the CPC. Use alongside virtualization.platform.serial_number for cross-platform consumers.

**[17] `virtualization.platform.firmware.version`:** The firmware or microcode version as reported by the platform management interface. For IBM Z this corresponds to the driver or MCL level reported by the HMC. No equivalent exists in the upstream OTel base registry; this attribute is specific to the virtualization schema.

**[18] `virtualization.platform.id`:** An opaque platform-specific identifier that uniquely identifies this physical computing platform. Prefer host.id for cross-platform compatibility; use this attribute when the management domain requires the platform-internal UUID.

**[19] `virtualization.platform.serial_number`:** The hardware serial number as reported by the platform management interface. Supplements host.id for platforms where the serial number and the management UUID differ.

**[20] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the specific hypervisor or partitioning technology managing this platform (e.g. ibm.prsm, ibm.zvm, vmware.esxi).

**[21] `virtualization.platform.model`:** The model identifier of the platform hardware. Consumers should prefer host.type; this attribute is retained for implementations that need the platform-specific model string separately.

**[22] `virtualization.platform.name`:** The human-readable name as configured in the platform management interface. Consumers should prefer host.name as the primary name attribute; this attribute is retained for compatibility with implementations that populate both.

| Description | `mainframe.partition.type` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The workload category of the logical partition (LPAR), reflecting which operating environment it is configured to run. [28] | `general_purpose`; `linux_only`; `zvm` |
| Description | `virtualization.partition.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The human-readable name assigned to the partition. [29] | `LPAR1`; `PROD`; `LINUX01` |
| Description | `virtualization.partition.number` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | int | The partition number assigned by the virtualization platform. [30] | `1`; `2`; `15` |
| Description | `virtualization.partition.state` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operational state of the partition. [31] | `active`; `not_activated`; `stopped` |
| Description | `virtualization.partition.type` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The workload type or operational mode of the partition. [32] | `general_purpose`; `linux_only`; `ssc` |
| Description | `virtualization.system.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtualization system (hypervisor technology) managing this platform. [33] | `ibm.prsm`; `ibm.zvm`; `ibm.powervm` |

**[23] `virtualization.partition.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this partition within its virtualization platform. On IBM Z in PR/SM (classic) mode this is the partition object-id assigned by the HMC.

**[24] `virtualization.platform.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this physical computing platform within its management domain. For IBM Z this corresponds to the CPC (Central Processing Complex) object-id as reported by the HMC Web Services API. Alignment with OTel base registry: this attribute is functionally equivalent to `host.id`. Consumers that understand the generic host entity should prefer `host.id`; use this attribute when the management domain requires the platform-internal UUID specifically. In virtualization.platform metrics, `virtualization.platform.id` is used as the time-series discriminating attribute because the identity attribute of the `virtualization.platform` entity is `host.name` and the UUID is needed to uniquely identify the entity instance when metrics are aggregated across platforms with different name scopes.

**[25] `host.name`:** The name of the Central Processing Complex (CPC) that hosts this logical partition (LPAR). Corresponds to the virtualization.platform identity for cross-platform portability.

**[26] `mainframe.partition.name`:** The LPAR name as configured on the HMC. This is the primary human-readable identifier for the partition.

**[27] `mainframe.partition.number`:** The numeric partition index assigned by PR/SM. Used to correlate HMC data with SMF records and hardware event logs that reference partitions by number rather than by name.

**[28] `mainframe.partition.type`:** The workload category of the partition. Determines which processor types and software environments are licensed for this LPAR.

**[29] `virtualization.partition.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface, e.g., the HMC (Hardware Management Console) for IBM Z PR/SM partitions. On IBM Z, partition names are 1–8 uppercase alphanumeric characters.

**[30] `virtualization.partition.number`:** The numeric index identifying the partition within the platform. On IBM Z PR/SM (classic) mode, this corresponds to the LPAR number as reported by the HMC Web Services API.

**[31] `virtualization.partition.state`:** Reflects the current activation or execution state of the partition as reported by the virtualization platform management interface.

**[32] `virtualization.partition.type`:** Classifies the partition by the category of workload it is configured to run. On IBM Z, this maps to the partition type field on the HMC.

**[33] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the virtualization technology managing this partition. Use this attribute to discriminate partition metrics by platform — e.g. filter on "ibm.prsm" to isolate IBM Z LPAR metrics from generic virtualization partition metrics.

---

`mainframe.partition.type` has the following list of well-known values. If one of them applies, then the respective value MUST be used; otherwise, a custom value MAY be used.

| Value | Description | Stability |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `general_purpose` | General-purpose partition that can run any IBM Z operating system including z/OS, Linux on Z, or z/VM, using all licensed processor types. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `linux_only` | Linux-only partition restricted to running Linux on Z; cannot activate a z/OS or z/VM image. Uses only Integrated Facility for Linux (IFL) processors. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `ssc` | Secure Service Container (SSC) partition for IBM Z security appliances; provides a hardware-isolated, tamper-evident execution environment. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `unknown` | The partition type is not known or could not be determined from the available HMC API response. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |
| `zvm` | Partition configured to host a z/VM hypervisor instance as its primary workload; can manage hundreds of guest virtual machines. | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) |

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

Mainframe refinement of virtualization.resource_pool for an IBM Z shared processor pool. A shared processor pool defines a capacity boundary for a group of physical processor engines (CP, IFL, zIIP, ICF) shared by logical partitions, directly analogous to virtualization.resource_pool in the generic virtualization schema.

**Type:** `virtualization.resource_pool`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Role | Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | `virtualization.resource_pool.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The human-readable name assigned to the virtualization resource pool. [34] | `high-priority-pool`; `linux-pool`; `Default Shared Pool` |
| Description | `mainframe.cpu.type` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The type of mainframe processor within the Central Processing Complex (CPC). [35] | `all`; `cp`; `icf` |
| Description | `virtualization.resource_pool.id` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | Unique identifier for the virtualization resource pool. [36] | `respool-001`; `8c3f2a1b-4d56-4e78-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` |
| Description | `virtualization.system.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtualization system (hypervisor technology) managing this platform. [37] | `ibm.prsm`; `ibm.zvm`; `ibm.powervm` |

**[34] `virtualization.resource_pool.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface. For VMware vSphere this is the resource pool name in vCenter. For IBM Z PR/SM this corresponds to the shared processor pool name as reported by the HMC Web Services API.

**[35] `mainframe.cpu.type`:** The type of processor engines managed by this shared pool. Maps to the processor-type property of the HMC Web Services API shared-processor- pool object.

**[36] `virtualization.resource_pool.id`:** A platform-specific opaque identifier for the resource pool. For VMware vSphere this is the resource pool MoRef ID. For IBM Z PR/SM this is the shared processor pool object-id reported by the HMC Web Services API.

**[37] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the virtualization technology owning this resource pool. Filter on "ibm.prsm" to isolate IBM Z shared processor pool metrics.

Mainframe refinement of virtualization.vm for an IBM z/VM guest virtual machine. A z/VM guest is a virtual machine managed by the z/VM Control Program (CP), running Linux on Z or z/OS, directly analogous to virtualization.vm in the generic virtualization schema.

**Type:** `virtualization.vm`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Role | Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | `virtualization.vm.id` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | Unique identifier for the virtual machine instance. [47] | `vm-0abc1234`; `8c3f2a1b-4d56-4e78-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` |
| Description | `mainframe.zvm.guest.userid` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The z/VM user identifier (userid) of the guest virtual machine. [48] | `LINUXVM1`; `PRODDB01`; `DEVGUEST` |
| Description | `mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the z/VM hypervisor instance (the LPAR running z/VM). [49] | `ZVMPROD`; `ZVMTEST`; `VMDEV01` |
| Description | `virtualization.system.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtualization system (hypervisor technology) managing this platform. [50] | `ibm.prsm`; `ibm.zvm`; `ibm.powervm` |
| Description | `virtualization.vm.cpu.count` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | int | The number of virtual CPUs (vCPUs) allocated to the virtual machine. [51] | `1`; `2`; `4`; `8` |
| Description | `virtualization.vm.instance_id` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The cloud or platform provider's instance identifier for the virtual machine. [52] | `i-0abc123def456789`; `1234567890abcdef0` |
| Description | `virtualization.vm.machine_type` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The machine type or hardware profile assigned to the virtual machine. [53] | `n1-standard-2`; `t3.medium`; `9175-ME1` |
| Description | `virtualization.vm.memory.size` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | int | The amount of memory allocated to the virtual machine, in mebibytes (MiB). [54] | `1024`; `4096`; `16384` |
| Description | `virtualization.vm.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The human-readable name assigned to the virtual machine. [55] | `my-web-server`; `prod-db-01`; `test-vm` |
| Description | `virtualization.vm.nested_virtualization.enabled` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | boolean | Indicates whether nested virtualization is enabled on this virtual machine. [56] | |
| Description | `virtualization.vm.state` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operational state of the virtual machine. | `running`; `stopped`; `paused` |

**[47] `virtualization.vm.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this virtual machine within the hypervisor. Analogous to `host.id` for physical machines or a container ID for containers.

**[48] `mainframe.zvm.guest.userid`:** The z/VM user directory identifier for this guest. Maps to the `zvm-guest-name` field of the HMC logical-partition object. This is the z/VM equivalent of `virtualization.vm.name`.

**[49] `mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.name`:** The LPAR name of the z/VM hypervisor hosting this guest. Used to correlate guests with their hypervisor instance.

**[50] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the virtualization technology managing this VM. Use this attribute to discriminate VM metrics by platform — e.g. filter on "ibm.zvm" to isolate z/VM guest metrics.

**[51] `virtualization.vm.cpu.count`:** The number of virtual CPUs visible to the guest operating system. This may differ from the number of physical CPUs on the underlying host.

**[52] `virtualization.vm.instance_id`:** A provider-assigned instance identifier, distinct from the hypervisor's own identifier (`virtualization.vm.id`). For example, on AWS this would be the EC2 instance ID; on IBM Z HMC DPM mode it would be the partition object-id.

**[53] `virtualization.vm.machine_type`:** A string identifying the virtual machine's hardware configuration class as defined by the hypervisor or cloud provider. For IBM Z DPM partitions this corresponds to the partition type profile.

**[54] `virtualization.vm.memory.size`:** The total memory allocation visible to the guest operating system, expressed in mebibytes (MiB). This is the configured allocation, not necessarily the currently consumed amount.

**[55] `virtualization.vm.name`:** The name as configured in the hypervisor management interface. Names are not guaranteed to be unique across hypervisors; use `virtualization.vm.id` for unambiguous identification.

**[56] `virtualization.vm.nested_virtualization.enabled`:** When `true`, the virtual machine is configured to expose virtualization extensions to its guest operating system, allowing a hypervisor to run inside the VM. Not all hypervisors or platforms support this capability.

## `refinement.mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.virtualization.hypervisor`

Refines upstream entity: `virtualization.hypervisor`

**Status:** ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue)

Mainframe refinement of virtualization.hypervisor for the z/VM Control Program (CP). z/VM is a Type-1 software hypervisor that runs on IBM Z hardware (bare-metal or inside a PR/SM LPAR) and manages hundreds to thousands of guest virtual machines, directly analogous to virtualization.hypervisor in the generic virtualization schema.

**Type:** `virtualization.hypervisor`

**Requirement Level:** `Recommended`

**Attributes:**

| Role | Key | Stability | [Requirement Level](https://opentelemetry.io/docs/specs/semconv/general/attribute-requirement-level/) | Value Type | Description | Example Values |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Identity | `virtualization.hypervisor.id` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | Unique identifier for the hypervisor instance. [57] | `8c3f2a1b-4d56-4e78-9f01-2a3b4c5d6e7f` |
| Description | `mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the z/VM hypervisor instance (the LPAR running z/VM). [58] | `ZVMPROD`; `ZVMTEST`; `VMDEV01` |
| Description | `virtualization.hypervisor.state` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The operational state of the hypervisor. | `active`; `inactive`; `unknown` |

| Description | `virtualization.hypervisor.version` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The version string of the hypervisor software. [60] | `6.4.0`; `2024.1.1`; `4.2.1-release` |
| Description | `virtualization.system.name` | ![Development](https://img.shields.io/badge/-development-blue) | `Recommended` | string | The name of the virtualization system (hypervisor technology) managing this platform. [61] | `ibm.prsm`; `ibm.zvm`; `ibm.powervm` |

**[57] `virtualization.hypervisor.id`:** A UUID or other platform-specific opaque identifier that uniquely identifies this hypervisor instance within the virtualization platform.

**[58] `mainframe.zvm.hypervisor.name`:** The name of the LPAR hosting the z/VM hypervisor instance. Maps to the `name` field of the logical-partition HMC object.

**[59] `virtualization.hypervisor.type`:** Classifies the hypervisor by its position in the virtualization stack. Type-1 (bare-metal) hypervisors run directly on hardware; Type-2 (hosted) hypervisors run within a host operating system.

**[60] `virtualization.hypervisor.version`:** The version as reported by the hypervisor software itself. Format is hypervisor-specific and should be used for informational purposes and correlation with vendor release notes.

**[61] `virtualization.system.name`:** Identifies the specific hypervisor or partitioning technology in use. This attribute allows consumers to correlate platform-specific behaviour and capabilities when multiple virtualization technologies are observed in a mixed environment. No equivalent exists in the upstream OTel base registry; this attribute is specific to the virtualization schema.
